linear and mixed-integer models · one command line

Models that are checked before they are solved, and checked again after.

cancho-solve reads a small text model, refuses a bad one with a rule tag and the line that fixes it, solves it, and solve verify re-checks any claimed answer without the search. Standard input, JSON out, no network.

Try itWatch it runRead the stories

What it does

{"error":"solve.unbounded-domain"}repair: var x : real 0..10;

It says no, with the fix

A refusal is one JSON line on standard error: a rule tag, a message, the repair and the position. 19 rules, listed by solve introspect.

solve.row-violated: weight 11verified: the model and the claim

A second opinion

solve verify re-checks bounds, integrality, every row and the objective, from any solver’s answer, with code that shares nothing with the search.

dense = sparse

Two engines, one answer

A dense tableau and a sparse revised simplex solve the same models; a gate holds them to the same optimum on 104 LPs and 161 integer models.

Watch it run

Three sessions of the real binary. Nothing on this page is typed in: scripts/site.py runs solve on the files of docs/examples and prints what came back.

the same runs, replayed here
A bakery, an LP
# 40 kg flour, 8 kg butter, 10 oven hours: how many loaves and trays of croissants?
$ solve run < bakery.sol
{"status":"optimal","objective":148.8,"x":{"loaf":8.8,"tray":2.4},"verified":true,"max_violation":0.0,"stats":{"iterations":2,"rows":3,"columns":2}}
A van, and a second opinion
# a courier van, six parcels, 15 kg: which to take (each whole or not at all)
$ solve run < van.sol
{"status":"optimal","objective":21.0,"bound":21.0,"x":{"take[0]":0.0,"take[1]":1.0,"take[2]":1.0,"take[3]":1.0,"take[4]":1.0,"take[5]":0.0},"verified":true,"max_violation":0.0,"stats":{"iterations":6,"rows":1,"columns":6,"nodes":7,"branched":4,"method":"dense"}}
# a second opinion that shares no code with the search: the model, a line ---, the claimed answer
$ (cat van.sol; echo ---; solve run < van.sol) | solve verify
{"status":"verified","objective":21.0,"objective_checked":true,"tolerance":0.000001,"max_bound_violation":0.0,"max_integrality_violation":0.0,"max_row_violation":0.0,"variables":6,"rows":1,"proves":"feasibility and the objective value, not optimality"}
# the same claim with the 12 kg parcel added by hand
$ (cat van.sol; echo ---; <the answer with take[0] changed to 1>) | solve verify
{"error":"solve.row-violated","message":"a constraint does not hold at the claimed values","repair":"the solution is infeasible; solve again","count":2,"violations":[{"rule":"solve.row-violated","what":"weight","value":11.0,"limit":0.000027},{"rule":"solve.objective-mismatch","what":"objective","value":4.0,"limit":0.000026}]}
# exit status 2
A refusal and its repair
# a variable with no bounds is refused by the checker, before any solver sees it
$ solve check < unbounded.sol
{"error":"solve.unbounded-domain","message":"a variable has no bounds","repair":"write the bounds: var x : real 0..10;","at":{"line":2,"col":5}}
# exit status 2
# the repair is a line of the model: give the bounds, and it runs

Recorded from real runs, not a live session. For a solution of more than eight entries the zero entries are left out and the cut is marked with an ellipsis; every other byte is as printed.

Stories, from a bakery to a refusal

A bakery, a courier van, a night rota, two depots, an electric-vehicle depot overnight and a shop floor that says no: each asks a little more of solve, and every number and figure is drawn from a run.

Read the storiesSee every command

How it works

A model becomes a flat list of variables and rows. An LP is solved by a dual simplex, dense or sparse; a model with bool or int variables by branch and bound over the same simplex. Anything it cannot accept comes back with its repair.

In words: a model goes to check, then to run, then to an answer; verify reads the model and the answer again. A model the tool cannot accept is refused with a rule tag, a position and a repair; you fix the line and try again.

Measured, not promised

168test LPs agree with HiGHS
194generated MIPs agree with HiGHS and enumeration, 142 also with CP-SAT and SCIP
13,414runs of mutated and cut inputs reach no panic
868checks of the verifier, accepting what is feasible and refusing each fault by its tag

Counts from the gates’ own last lines on 2026-11-05, one machine; the commands are in the README and docs/design.md. On the generated families of scripts/bench_highs.py the dual simplex takes 0.5x to 1.4x of HiGHS’s dual simplex; the sparse engine is 0.4x to 1.5x of CLP on transportation and assignment, and CLP is far faster on large min-cost flows (design.md sections 17 and 18).

Try it

Build it from source with the compiler written in cancho; cancho.toml pins the revision.

git clone https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho                  # the compiler and its std
git clone https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-solve && cd cancho-solve
# build the compiler at the revision cancho.toml pins (scripts/build-standalone.sh builds the one written in cancho), then:
cancho build --bin solve                                         # writes build/solve
build/solve run < docs/examples/bakery.sol

No release is published today, so the source is the way in. These steps are the README’s; the page does not re-run them.

What is not claimed

Not CP

Constraint programming (all_different, cumulative, element) is reserved in the language and not built.

MIP trails the best

Branch and bound has no cuts or presolve: it needs more nodes than HiGHS and SCIP, and falls behind on larger instances (design.md section 19.5).

Verify does not prove optimality

solve verify proves feasibility within a tolerance and the objective value; a feasible poor point verifies. Optimality is held by oracles in the gates, not by the verb.

One machine, generated models

Every timing is one machine and generated or textbook families, not MIPLIB. The auto choice between the dense and sparse engine is fitted on those families only.
